bib.title: Intelligence per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency of Local AI

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Intelligence per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency of Local AI", Saad-Falcon, Narayan et al. (Stanford, Together AI; Ré, Hennessy, Mirhoseini senior authors). Preprint, arXiv 2511.07885v7 [cs.DC], dated 1 Oct 2026, 37 pages. Source file: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/07-inference-engineering/sources/saad-falcon-2025-intelligence-per-watt.pdf. This is v7, so it carries post-2025 additions (OpenClaw and similar agent stacks, the multi-turn appendix).

COVERAGE: I read lines 1-700 and 760-1843 of the 1843-line extraction at /tmp/potw-saad-falcon-2025-intelligence-per-watt.txt. That covers the body, limitations, future work and all of Appendices B to E. I skipped lines 700-760, the middle of the references, which hold no results. I did not read the whole text. The extraction is clean, with garbled layout only in Table 4 and the prompt listings. I did not run figure extraction, so figure notes come from the captions in the text. Page numbers below are PDF pages.

CLAIMS (ranked)

1. Efficiency per watt rose 5.3x from 2023 to 2025, but the 3.1x model / 1.7x hardware split reverses under per-joule accounting.
   - number: 5.3x; 3.1x model and 1.7x hardware per watt; 18.0x per joule (3.1x model, 5.9x hardware)
   - setup: Best local LM (≤20B active parameters) on the best available accelerator for each year. The pairs are Mixtral-8x7B on Quadro RTX 6000 (2023), Llama-3.1-8B on RTX 6000 Ada (2024) and GPT-OSS-120B on Apple M4 Max (2025). IPW is mean accuracy divided by mean power. Single-turn chat and reasoning mix, bs=1.
   - quote: "accuracy per watt has improved 5.3× over this two-year period: in 2023, MIXTRAL-8X7B-V0.1 on NVIDIA QUADRO RTX 6000 achieved 7.92×10 −4 accuracy per watt; by 2024, LLAMA-3.1-8B-INSTRUCT on NVIDIA RTX 6000 ADA reached 1.80×10 −3 (a 2.27× year-over-year gain); and in 2025, GPT-OSS-120B on APPLE M4 MAX achieved 4.18×10 −3 (a 2.32× gain)."
   - where: p8, Table 2 on p7
   - Also: "Model progress dominates per-watt efficiency; hardware progress dominates per-joule efficiency, because newer accelerators (HBM3e bandwidth, dedicated tensor units) reduce latency as well as power." Fig 3 is on p8.
   - Inconsistency: Fig 3's caption says 3.0x from models and "18.0x over 16 months". The text and footnote say 3.1x and "two-year". Fig 3 and App E.3 use a different hardware set (A100, H100, H200, L40S), so it is not the same series as Table 2.

2. Local accelerators trail cloud accelerators on identical models by 1.4x on IPW and 1.6-2.3x on IPJ (B200 vs M4 Max). SambaNova SN40L reaches 1.78x IPW and 6.5-7.4x IPJ over M4 Max.
   - number: 1.40x; 1.6-2.3x; 1.78x; 6.5-7.4x
   - setup: Qwen3 4B to 32B and GPT-OSS-20B/120B, bs=1 on both sides, vLLM, mean ± 1σ over 3-5 runs. Energy is accelerator-only (NVML on B200, `powermetrics` GPU power on M4 Max).
   - quote: "For QWEN3-32B, the B200 achieves (2.75±0.14)×10 −3 intelligence per watt compared to (1.97±0.24)×10 −3 for the M4 Max." Also: "(3.12±0.38)×10 −4 versus (4.23±0.45)×10 −5 for GPT-OSS-120B."
   - where: p33, Tables 13-14
   - Paper's explanation: HBM3e at 4.8-8 TB/s versus 546 GB/s unified memory. The gap is larger per joule "because cloud accelerators not only consume less power per unit of accuracy but also complete queries faster". This is asserted, not isolated experimentally.

3. Batching is worth 11-20x per-joule efficiency on cloud hardware, and power grows sublinearly with batch size.
   - number: 11.2-19.7x; 255 W to 883 W; Qwen3-8B 6,449 J to 548 J
   - setup: NVIDIA B200, bs=1 versus bs=64, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B and GPT-OSS-120B. Single ablation.
   - quote: "Per-query energy drops 12–20× at bs=64 (e.g., QWEN3-8B: 6,449J → 548J) while GPU power scales sublinearly (255W at bs=1 to 883W at bs=64)."
   - where: p35, Table 15
   - Why it matters: this supports the utilization / goodput argument directly. Idle power is amortised across concurrent requests, so the headline 1.4x local-versus-cloud gap is at bs=1, the cloud's worst case. Text says "11–20×", the caption "12–20×", and the table 11.2-19.7x.

4. Hybrid routing saves 60-80% of energy, compute and cost, but most of the saving comes from model size, not hardware.
   - number: oracle 80.4% energy, 77.3% compute, 73.8% cost. The 80%-accurate router gets 64.3% / 61.8% / 59.0%. The 60%-accurate router gets 48.4% / 46.7% / 44.5%.
   - setup: Simulation of 80.2M queries over 24 h. Four local models (Qwen3-4B/8B/14B, GPT-OSS-20B) on M4 Max at bs=1. Cloud baseline is Qwen3-235B on H200 at bs=16. Misrouted queries fall back to the cloud model. Cost uses OpenRouter prices from Aug 2025.
   - quote: "The dominant effect is the reduction in model size, not a hardware efficiency advantage."
   - where: p9, Fig 4
   - It is a simulation with a simulated router, and the energy is scaled from per-query measurements. The paper does not describe how the 80.2M-query energy is derived beyond that.

5. Local models answer 88.7% of single-turn queries under best-of-local routing. The best single model, GPT-OSS-120B, covers 71.4%.
   - number: 88.7%; 71.4%; WildChat 88.9% versus NaturalReasoning 64.9% (best single local LM)
   - setup: 20+ local models, 1M queries. Accuracy for WildChat is win-or-tie versus Qwen3-235B as judged by an LLM. The others are exact match or judge against ground truth.
   - quote: "Routing queries to the most appropriate local LM rather than using a single model achieves 88.7% overall coverage"
   - where: p7
   - Caveat the paper itself gives: best-of-local beating best-of-cloud is "a best-of-N selection effect" (20+ models versus 3).

6. FP16 to FP4 cuts energy 3-3.5x for about 2.5 pp accuracy per precision step.
   - number: 3-3.5x; ~2.5 pp. Example: Qwen3-14B on SuperGPQA 54.5 / 52.0 / 49.0% at FP16 / FP8 / FP4, a 3.23x energy reduction.
   - setup: Eight Qwen3 and Gemma models, energy on B200, replicated on M4 Max. 10,000 queries each on NaturalReasoning, SuperGPQA and MMLU-Pro.
   - quote: "QWEN3-14B at FP4 (49.0% accuracy) outperforms QWEN3-4B at FP16 (48.5% accuracy) on SuperGPQA"
   - where: p29

7. Serving framework barely moves the ranking.
   - number: 3-12% IPW shift; Kendall τ 0.87-0.93
   - setup: M4 Max, vLLM versus SGLang versus llama.cpp, four models
   - quote: "Absolute IPW values shift by 3–12% across frameworks, but relative rankings between model-hardware pairs are preserved"
   - where: p36, Table 16
   - Table 16 is four models on one device, but the τ claim says "across the broader 20+-model, 8-accelerator evaluation". That scope is not shown.

8. A phone-class chip (iPhone 16 Pro, A18 Pro) has about 7x the IPW of workstation GPUs, but that does not carry over to per joule.
   - number: 11.2-13.3×10⁻³ IPW; 7.2x versus M4 Max, 6.6x versus RTX 6000 Ada; 9-26x higher latency
   - setup: Qwen3-4B FP4 and other 4B-class models, ~12 W, 60 GB/s memory. Qwen3-4B FP4 accuracy is 38.0% on the phone versus 44.5% on the workstations.
   - quote: "the A18 Pro's 9–26× higher latency partially offsets its 20–25× lower power draw" (as printed: "reflecting that the A18 Pro's 9–26×higher latency partially offsets its 20–25×lower power")
   - where: p36, Table 17
   - Lesson: IPW rewards low power even when the device is slow, which is why the paper reports IPJ too.

9. Multi-turn agentic check: the patterns flip in opposite directions per watt and per joule.
   - number: cloud 2.4-3.0x better IPJ; M4 Max 3.7-3.8x better IPW; energy in kJ per query
   - setup: GAIA (165 queries) and TerminalBenchV2 (80 queries). Cloud is 8xH100 under vLLM at native precision. M4 Max runs GGUF quantised. Three runs.
   - quote: "We caution that 245 multi-turn queries is a small evaluation and view this experiment as a sanity check rather than a definitive characterization"
   - where: p37, Table 18
   - Cross-check: this contradicts the single-turn "local is worse per watt" headline. Here the 8-GPU node draws 1-1.6 kW, so power is compared at node level versus a single SoC.

10. Reasoning difficulty is the unsolved part: the hardest reasoning queries barely improved.
    - number: Level 4 improved only +23.8 pp (7.93% to 31.72%); Level 5 +1.5 pp (3.27% to 4.72%)
    - quote: "Level 4 improves by only +23.8 pp (7.93% to 31.72%), and level 5 remains largely unsolved with just +1.5 pp improvement (3.27% to 4.72%)."
    - where: p27-28. Local memory capacity grew about 126x from 2012 to 2025 (p7, p34).

11. The metric definitions are in a formula block.
    - APW = E[acc]/E[P]
    - APJ = E[acc]/E[P·τ]
    - Accuracy is binary. The ratio is of means, not a mean of ratios.
    - where: p3-4

12. Open-source versus closed-source gap (Table 11-12).
    - number: best local ≤20B active trails closed by 11-13% (text). Qwen3-235B average 71.8% versus GPT-5 77.9% in text; the table row says GPT-5 78.9%.
    - quote: "the best open-source model (QWEN3-235B-A22B) achieves 71.8% average accuracy across benchmarks, trailing the best closed-source model (GPT-5-2025-08-07, 77.9%) by 6.1 percentage points."
    - where: p29-31

LIMITS
- Authors concede in App. C: telemetry is software-based with 10-15% error; single-turn only; the judge is Qwen3-235B (a bias risk); hardware coverage is narrow; bs=1 is conservative for cloud; single runtime (vLLM); models and hardware are as of Oct 2025; DRAM/HBM price rises could slow local deployment.
- The authors also flag a Jevons-paradox concern they did not quantify.
- Inputs are capped at 32,000 characters. Long-context prefill and KV-cache pressure are not measured, and the paper names this as future work (p25).
- Power scope is the accelerator only: NVML, ROCm SMI, or `processor_power.actual` (the GPU subsystem, not the SoC package). Host CPU, DRAM, cooling and network are excluded, so the cloud-versus-local comparison is not wall power. Table 7 says the M4 Max Mac Studio is rated 480 W at the PSU.
- Accuracy is a binary win/tie against a reference (Qwen3-235B) for chat, which is lenient. "Success rate" is not human-judged quality.
- Table 2 pairs the best model with the best hardware per year, so model and hardware effects are not cross-validated.
- Inconsistencies spotted:
  - 3.0x versus 3.1x model gain (Fig 3 caption vs text).
  - Abstract "at least 1.4x" versus Fig 1 "1.5x".
  - Best-of-local SuperGPQA is 83.6% (p7) versus 77.0% (Fig 2 caption).
  - Architecture & engineering solvability is 41.5% (App B text) versus 40.8% (Table 4).
  - B200 Qwen3-8B IPJ is 8.71 (Table 14) versus 8.92 (Table 15).
  - Table 17 gives M4 Max power as 240 W, but Table 7 lists 480 W as the PSU rating.
  - The abstract's coverage rise of 23.2% to 71.3% uses a different definition from the 88.7% best-of-local figure.
- Dated: the models are Qwen3, GPT-OSS and Gemma3 as of Oct 2025. The GPT-5 / Gemini 2.5 / Sonnet 4.5 frontier references are old for a Nov 2026 reader.
- Not shown: any serving-system goodput or SLO analysis, speculative decoding, paged attention, power capping, cross-app local batching. The paper lists them as future work.

BUILDS ON
- Fernandez et al. 2025 (energy of LLM inference, cloud A100/H100).
- Samsi et al. 2023 ("From Words to Watts", 100 ms sampling).
- CodeCarbon (rejected: 15 s default sampling).
- Koomey et al. 2010 (performance-per-watt doubling every 1.5 years, 1946-2009).
- Strubell 2019, Patterson 2021 and Schwartz 2020 (Green AI).
- Routing: RouteLLM (Ong 2025), FrugalGPT (Chen 2023), RouterBench, RouterDC.
- Minions (Narayan 2025), SLED, SpecInfer.
- Zeus and uServe, named as complementary system-level work they did not vary.
- Eval: Anthropic Economic Index (Handa 2025), WildChat, NaturalReasoning, MMLU-Pro, SuperGPQA.

CODE: none beyond the metric formulas above and the harness link (https://github.com/HazyResearch/intelligence-per-watt). Sampling is at 50 ms with numerical integration, and each query is run 10 times and averaged (p5, p23-24).

FIGURES (captions in the extraction; not rendered)
- Fig 3 (p8): per-joule gain decomposition into model and hardware. It carries the "different metric, different answer" point.
- Fig 4 (p9): cumulative energy, compute and cost saved by routing over 24 h. It is the best visual for the hybrid-routing claim.
- Table 15 (p35): a table, but the clearest batching-versus-energy evidence.
- Fig 2 (p6): coverage per model, best-of-local versus best-of-cloud.
- Figs 6-7 (p27-28): difficulty slices.
- Fig 13 (p35): local memory growth.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table layouts in the text extraction are flattened (Table 2, 13, 14 read in order). I did not render any figure. Lines 700-760 (references) were not read.

SUGGESTED HOME (for the caller to decide): notes/01 "Throughput, cost and goodput" or "Utilization" can use claims 3 and 2 (batching amortises idle power; the local-versus-cloud gap is measured at bs=1). Claim 6 fits a quantization section. Claim 1 and the IPW/IPJ definitions fit a hardware or efficiency note.
